claim_scores.rationale: Answer demonstrates the default no-valset path by omitting `valset`, using `BetterTogether.compile(...)`, and asserting the resulting 9/1 split consistent with default `valset_ratio=0.1` and nonzero holdout behavior.
With a 10-example trainset, the program proves the default split yields 1 validation example and 9 remaining training examples via the final assertions.
The custom `CapturingOptimizer` records the `trainset` passed into `optimizer.compile`, and the answer asserts that length is 9, matching post-split training data.
The patched evaluator records dataset sizes, and the answer asserts evaluation sees size 1, showing validation uses the held-out set rather than the original trainset.
The answer captures two evaluation calls and asserts `seen_eval_sizes == [1, 1]`, matching baseline-plus-single-step evaluation on the same 1-example valset.
